per variable – the one corresponding to a satisfying assignment – and all
clause vertices are adjacent to at least one chosen vertex, giving a
dominating set of size ``m``.  Conversely, any dominating set of size ``m``
must contain exactly one of the two vertices for each variable (otherwise we
would need more than ``m`` vertices to dominate the isolated clause vertices).

We implement our own brute-force solvers for both problems directly from the

import itertools
import json
import random

from problems import ThreeSat, DominatingSet
from reduce import reduce


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# Brute-force solvers written from the problem definitions.

def brute_sat(instance):
    """Return True iff the 3-SAT instance is satisfiable."""
    ThreeSat.validate(instance)
    m = instance["num_vars"]
    clauses = instance["clauses"]
    for bits in itertools.product([False, True], repeat=m):
        good = True
        for clause in clauses:
            sat = False
            for lit in clause:
                val = bits[abs(lit) - 1]
                if (lit > 0 and val) or (lit < 0 and not val):
                    sat = True
                    break
            if not sat:
                good = False
                break
        if good:
            return True
    return False


def brute_ds(instance):
    """Return True iff the graph has a dominating set of size at most k."""
    DominatingSet.validate(instance)
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]
    if k < 0:
        return False
    if k >= n:
        return True
    adj = [set() for _ in range(n)]
    for u, v in edges:
        adj[u].add(v)
        adj[v].add(u)
    for size in range(0, k + 1):
        for comb in itertools.combinations(range(n), size):
            dominated = set(comb)
            for v in comb:
                dominated |= adj[v]
            if len(dominated) == n:
                return True
    return False


def ds_witness(instance):
    """Return a dominating set of size <= k, or None."""
    n, edges, k = instance["n"], instance["edges"], instance["k"]
    if k < 0:
        return None
    adj = [set() for _ in range(n)]
    for u, v in edges:
        adj[u].add(v)
        adj[v].add(u)
    for size in range(0, min(k, n) + 1):
        for comb in itertools.combinations(range(n), size):
            dominated = set(comb)
            for v in comb:
                dominated |= adj[v]
            if len(dominated) == n:
                return comb
    return None

    """All valid 3-literal clauses over variables 1..m."""
    clauses = []
